root_cause_identified.expected_solution: The prototype-pollution sink is not in Express or body-parser; it is in the transitive query-string library qs (lib/parse.js). At tag v6.9.6 the recursive key-expansion routine parseObject rebuilds a bracket-nested object from the innermost segment outward and, in its final branch, executes `obj[cleanRoot] = leaf` with no check that cleanRoot is the special prototype key. A submitted key of foo[__proto__][isAdmin] is expanded so that __proto__ is assigned as a key on a plain object, which mutates Object.prototype for the whole process. The JSON body path uses a different parser and never calls parseObject, which is why only the form-urlencoded path pollutes. The agent must attribute the sink to qs and name parseObject's unguarded assignment.
evaluation_criteria: Attributes the sink to qs (the transitive dependency), NOT Express or body-parser
Names the recursive key-expansion routine in qs's parse module and the unguarded final assignment of the decoded key onto a plain object
Explains that no exclusion of the __proto__ key exists at v6.9.6, so the prototype gets polluted

Explains the two independent paths that reach the sink: body-parser's extended urlencoded parser (dynamic require of qs) and Express's built-in query layer (qs.parse), and why plain import-following from the app does not reach it

patch_lands_at_fix_site.expected_solution: The agent leaves an uncommitted diff in /workspace/qs that modifies lib/parse.js at the recursive key-expansion routine (parseObject), matching the upstream fix (qs commit 8b4cc14cda94). A diff that only touches express or body-parser, or that changes the route handler / middleware option, is not the correct site.
evaluation_criteria: git diff in the qs workspace repo shows a modification to lib/parse.js
The change is in qs, not express or body-parser
No new files; an in-place edit of the existing recursive parse routine

patch_excludes_prototype_key.expected_solution: The patch prevents the special __proto__ key from being assigned during recursive key expansion, exactly as the upstream fix does with `else if (cleanRoot !== '__proto__')` so the prototype key is ignored like any other absent key. Equivalent handling that skips assigning the prototype key onto the built object is acceptable; a blanket removal of nested parsing or an app-layer sanitizer is not.
evaluation_criteria: The prototype key is excluded from assignment during key expansion rather than assigned onto the object
The fix is scoped to the recursive parse routine, not the app handler or the middleware option
